The structural fix is to make the reattachment **global**: re-elect the entire trunk attachment point (a hub). For each candidate hub v, build a complete alternative solution "shared src→v trunk + per-dst directed tails v→dst", evaluate it on the exact union-cost objective, and keep the best across all hubs — then run the per-dst tail sweep on the winner. This reaches topologies the Steiner/anneal basin cannot (single shared trunk + star tails), and it's cheap on region-sized graphs: one forward Dijkstra from src (all prefixes), one reversed Dijkstra per dst (all tails), one `sol_cost` evaluation per hub.

Key structural differences from the two failed attempts:
- **Global hub re-election** replaces the incumbent trunk wholesale: every dst is reattached at hub v via `src→v` (shared, charged once) + fresh directed `v→dst` tails. This constructs complete alternative topologies the anneal basin cannot express, so it can produce a cost strictly below the annealed optimum rather than the same 0.001585 value.
- **Whole-solution acceptance**: the hub trial replaces all dst paths simultaneously, so it isn't blocked by per-dst local optimality of the incumbent.
- **Bounded compute**: one forward Dijkstra (all prefixes), ≤25 reversed Dijkstras (all tails per dst), ≤25 hub evaluations, ≤3 polish sweeps — negligible against the 600 s limit.
- The incumbent is preserved whenever no hub beats it (strict improvement gate), and the normal `record` return path is untouched.
